rationale: Option A reports the unscorable preferences with a count, excludes them from comparisons, and warns against reading them as null effects. That is the calibrated, hedged treatment this persona favors. Option B marks the entire multi-turn behavioral column as incoherent, which overgeneralizes because other behavioral preferences were scorable. It also adds appendix transcripts, which costs more effort for a pragmatic, resource-conscious evaluator.
